subject: Newton Health onramp: environment gating matrix, API keys & peering asks
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Ng <alice.ng@newtonhealth.com>, Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@newtonhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Newton Health MAP — initial environment gating & asks

Hi Alice / Diego,

Following our demo last week, attached is a first-pass mutual action plan focused on the POC environment gating we discussed. To keep the evaluation window tight and predictable, we need to align on four technical acceptance items up front:

- Org setup: a Redwood service account in your org with Viewer + NetworkUser for peering validation (we'll provide a template).
- API keys: ephemeral API keys for the POC (30-day TTL) and a stable service account for automated runs.
- IP allowlist: one or two /28 CIDRs (or a range) to whitelist in your firewall for control-plane callbacks.
- VPC peering: cross-account peering or shared VPC; we'll send a simple diagram and routing notes.

I pulled these into the attached MAP spreadsheet (tab: gating_matrix). Can you confirm who on your infra team owns the peering and allowlist changes, and whether ProcureOps should be cc'd for procurement timing?

Suggested timeline (we can compress):
- Day 0: mutual ack + identify infra contacts
- Day 1-3: service account & ephemeral keys provisioned
- Day 4-7: IP allowlist & VPC peering done, smoke tests
- Day 8-12: model eval + performance baseline

If that looks good I'll loop in Neha and Soojin for the technical runbook and a brief peering checklist.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alice Ng <alice.ng@newtonhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 10:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Newton Health MAP — initial environment gating & asks

Ben — quick technical notes to add to the MAP before we hand it to Newton infra:

1) API keys: we'll deliver two artifacts: (a) ephemeral trial key (scoped to the trial tenant, rotates automatically), (b) service-account key for CI / load tests (recommend RSA key + KMS). Ephemeral key TTL = 30 days by default, can reduce to 7 days if their security wants it.

2) IP allowlist: Redwood control-plane egress will come from the hosted control-plane ranges: 34.72.48.0/23 and 18.196.64.0/22 (example ranges). Ask Newton to allow those plus a small set of ephemeral worker CIDRs we'll share after peering is established.

3) VPC peering options: we can do either (A) cross-account peering (fast, one-time routing), or (B) PrivateLink-style NAT tunnel if peering isn't allowed. Provide both instructions; cross-account peering preferred for performance.

4) Test checklist: Service account SAML group, IAM policy snippet, route-table update confirmation, ability to ping internal test endpoint (10.200.100.5:5000) once peered.

I'll update the MAP spreadsheet and attach an example ephemeral-key-template.txt and vpc-peering-diagram.png.

— Neha
From: Alice Ng <alice.ng@newtonhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@newtonhealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Newton Health MAP — initial environment gating & asks

Ben / Neha — thanks for the clear breakdown. A few clarifying points from our side:

- Peering owner: that's Diego (network team). He can action cross-account peering but will need the exact route-table changes and the peering CIDR.
- IP allowlist: our security team prefers a short-lived CIDR (we can allocate a /28 in our infra project). They also require a list of outbound domains for any callbacks.
- Procurement: I looped in ProcureOps for the reserved capacity discussion; they asked for an MSA redline and the MAP to show milestone-based acceptance.

Questions:
1) Can Redwood provide an inbound healthcheck endpoint we can use for validation after peering?
2) If peering takes longer than expected, can we temporarily validate over a VPN tunnel?

Assignees:
- Diego: peering + route-table (internal)
- Alice: security signoff on IP ranges
- Procurement: timeline for POC spend approval

We'll review the attached MAP and get back with precise CIDRs by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Alice
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Ng <alice.ng@newtonhealth.com>, Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@newtonhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Newton Health MAP — initial environment gating & asks

Appreciate the quick reply, Alice and team. Answers inline and an updated MAP (v1) attached.

- Healthcheck endpoint: yes — we'll publish a short-lived HTTP health endpoint (https://health.redwood.ai/newton-poc/ready) that your infra can curl post-peering. We'll provide a signed HMAC token for verification.
- Temporary VPN: absolutely — we've used a lightweight IPsec tunnel in the past for customers who couldn't peer immediately. We'll provide the tunnel parameters.

Proposed compressed timeline (if procurement and infra align):
- Day 0 (Wed): Confirm CIDR + peering owner (Diego)
- Day 1 (Thu): Redwood provides ephemeral key + service account template; Newton creates service account
- Day 2-3 (Fri–Mon): Peering + route updates; smoke test using healthcheck
- Day 4–7 (Tue–Fri): Run baseline evals; share latency/cost report

If we hit a gating delay on peering beyond Day 3 we fallback to VPN for the smoke tests so the eval window stays on track.

Next meeting: 30 min alignment call tomorrow 09:00 PT to confirm CIDRs and procurement ETA. I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Ben
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Ng <alice.ng@newtonhealth.com>, Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@newtonhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 09:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Newton Health MAP — initial environment gating & asks

Diego / Alice — adding the peering acceptance checklist we'll use during handoff:

1) Confirm peering request created with Newton account ID + region.
2) Validate route tables: Redwood announces 10.150.0.0/16 (worker CIDR). Please confirm no overlapping CIDRs.
3) Security groups: allow 10.150.10.0/24 -> 10.200.100.5:5000 (healthcheck).
4) BGP/route propagation: ensure route table propagation is complete and we can traceroute to the test endpoint.
5) Post-peering smoke: curl health endpoint + run a 100-request latency sample.

I attached the vpc-peering-diagram.png and the ephemeral-key-template.txt to the MAP spreadsheet. If Diego wants, we can hold a 15-min runbook walk-through immediately after the calendar slot Ben proposed.

— Soojin
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Ng <alice.ng@newtonhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@newtonhealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, ProcureOps <sourcing@procureops.io>
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Newton Health MAP — initial environment gating & asks

Thanks everyone — quick procurement + project note from my side:

- Procurement: ProcureOps, can you confirm the POC budget and whether a short-term card authorization works to start the trial? If not, we'll share a simplified SOW and milestone-based invoicing tied to the MAP.
- Project gating: once the CIDRs are confirmed, we'll treat Day 0 as the mutual-go and lock the MAP milestones. I'll track the acceptance checklist in the shared Drive folder and update HS-23456789 in HubSpot so all milestones appear on the deal.

Action items (owners):
- Diego: confirm CIDRs and peering window (due: EOD 2026-08-06)
- Alice: security approval for ephemeral key TTL (due: 2026-08-06)
- ProcureOps: procurement path + POC spend approval (due: 2026-08-07)
- Neha / Soojin: provide runbook + ephemeral key samples (done)

I'll follow up after the alignment call and push a short summary to the Drive link.

Best,
Marissa
